sections.h2: Where is Eagle, Idaho and how did it start?
sections.html:
Eagle is a city in Ada County, about ten miles northwest of downtown Boise. It had 30,346 residents in the 2020 census, and the Census Bureau estimated 34,658 on July 1, 2025.

The area was first settled in 1863, when Truman Coe Catlin settled Eagle Island, and the Eagle community was established in the 1870s. Eagle Island State Park, nearby, has a swimming beach, trails, disc golf and winter sports. The city covers about 29.4 square miles according to the Census Bureau figures that Wikipedia cites, at an elevation of 2,599 feet.

Before you list, know your lot's zoning, your flood zone status and any subdivision rules that apply, because those details differ from one lot to the next.

  • County: Ada
  • Distance to downtown Boise: about 10 miles
  • 2020 census population: 30,346
  • Estimated population on July 1, 2025: 34,658 (Census Bureau)

sections.h2: What does Eagle's economy look like?
sections.html:
Eagle has a notable retiree presence, including many retired public servants from California. Wikipedia reports that Eagle is home to many retired civil servants, especially police officers and firefighters from California, and that the Los Angeles Times described California pension money from CalPERS as the lifeblood of the economy in Eagle.

Sellers here may be downsizing, moving closer to family or settling an estate. A person who inherits an Eagle house from a retired parent may live in another state and want a closing that does not require repeated trips. A cash sale can be handled with fewer in-person steps than a typical listing.

Most of Eagle is in the West Ada School District, with a small part in the Boise School District. Check which district your house is in before you quote it to a buyer.

sections.h2: How does the Boise River floodplain affect an Eagle house?
sections.html:
If your house is in the mapped floodplain, flood rules apply to it, and a buyer's lender may require flood insurance. The City of Eagle's floodplain brochure says a floodplain development permit must be obtained before any construction or development begins in the floodplain, including buildings, filling, grading, paving or excavation. The rule comes from the Flood Hazard Overlay District in Title 10 of the Eagle City Code.

The brochure adds that standard homeowners insurance does not generally cover flood loss, and that Eagle participates in the National Flood Insurance Program, which makes federally backed flood insurance available. It says flood insurance is required in certain cases, such as buying a home with a federally backed mortgage.

For a seller, the useful step is to ask the city for the elevation certificate and permit history before you list. A buyer who learns about the floodplain only after an inspection may walk away. Giving the paperwork up front avoids that.

sections.h2: How is a house in Eagle affected by the weather?
sections.html:
Eagle has cold winters and dry summers. Wikipedia notes that winters average about ten inches of snow, and the winter low temperature averages 30.6 degrees Fahrenheit.

The practical checklist is short. Have the roof, heating and cooling equipment checked, look at the grading around the foundation, and confirm how the lot is irrigated. A house near the river deserves an extra look at drainage and any signs of past water. If you find an issue, a cash sale lets you sell without fixing it first, while a listing buyer will usually ask you to repair it or lower the price.

sections.h2: When are property taxes due on an Eagle house?
sections.html:
Eagle houses are taxed through Ada County, so the county treasurer's dates apply. Ada County lists December 20 as the due date for the full-year payment or the first half and June 20 for the second half.

The Idaho State Tax Commission says the assessor estimates what a typical buyer would pay as of January 1, notices usually go out by the first Monday in June, and an appeal to the county Board of Equalization is due by the fourth Monday in June. The state also reports that each taxing district can raise the property tax part of its budget by no more than 3 percent unless voters approve more or new construction and annexation apply.

  • Assessment notice: usually by the first Monday in June
  • Board of Equalization appeal: by the fourth Monday in June
  • First half or full payment: December 20
  • Second half: June 20
  • Deed recording fee at the Ada County Recorder: $15.00

The Ada County Recorder's Office is at 200 W Front Street, Room 1207, Boise, and is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Your closing agent will normally handle recording for you.

sections.h2: What does Idaho law require an Eagle seller to disclose?
sections.html:
Idaho requires most residential sellers to deliver a property condition disclosure form. Section 55-2504 of the Idaho Code applies to anyone who intends to transfer residential real property, including non-owner-occupied rental property.

Section 55-2505 lists the exceptions. Among them are transfers by a fiduciary during the administration of a decedent's estate, transfers from a decedent's estate, foreclosure transfers, transfers to a spouse or lineal relative, and a transfer by someone who inherited the property and has not occupied it as a personal residence in the past year.

Eagle sellers should keep one more point in mind. Section 55-2508 asks the seller about the property's condition, and a house in or near the floodplain raises questions that fit that form. Answer them honestly and attach the elevation certificate if you have one.

sections.h2: Can an Eagle owner rent the house short term before selling?
sections.html:
Idaho law limits what cities can do about short-term rentals. Senate Bill 1162 of 2025 amended section 67-6539 of the Idaho Code so that neither a county nor a city may enact or enforce an ordinance that has the express or practical effect of prohibiting short-term rentals.

Before you list a house that has been rented by the night, ask the City of Eagle and Ada County about any rules that apply, and gather the booking history a buyer will want to see.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale a good fit in Eagle?
sections.html:
A cash sale fits when you need a firm closing date or want to avoid repairs and showings. In Eagle that often includes houses that come with these circumstances:

  • An estate sale where the heirs live out of state
  • A house with floodplain paperwork or older systems that would slow a loan approval
  • A rental that has lost its tenant
  • A move for work or health reasons

Cash Home Buyers makes as-is offers with no commissions and no closing costs charged to you by us. If the number does not suit you, you owe nothing. Compare it with what a listing would net before you decide.

faqs.q: How far is Eagle from Boise?
faqs.a: Eagle is about ten miles northwest of downtown Boise, in Ada County.

faqs.q: Do I need flood insurance on an Eagle house?
faqs.a: It depends on whether the house is in the mapped floodplain and on the buyer's lender. The City of Eagle says flood insurance is required in certain cases, such as buying a home with a federally backed mortgage.

faqs.q: When are Ada County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Ada County lists December 20 for the full-year payment or the first half, and June 20 for the second half.
Most of Eagle is in the West Ada School District, with a small part in the Boise School District. Confirm the district for your address.

faqs.q: Do I need to complete a disclosure form to sell my Eagle house?
faqs.a: Usually yes, under Idaho Code 55-2504, unless an exemption in section 55-2505 applies, such as a transfer by a fiduciary in an estate.
